title: SSE reassembly edge-cases — debuglog and repro
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal log while chasing a flakey streaming issue where chunk reassembly fails under moderate backpressure (prod-ish load). Goal is a minimal repro, commands I tried, raw snippets, hypotheses, and short next steps. Not a post-mortem — just breadcrumbs for follow-up and handoff.

Symptom summary (observed):
- Client sees truncated event frames (partial JSON) intermittently (~1 in 200 request streams) when server is under sustained concurrency and with continuous small token bursts.
- Failures cluster after ~30s of heavy traffic on a single model route.
- When failure occurs, server logs show no exception but downstream proxy (nginx ingress) reports "upstream prematurely closed connection" around same timestamp.

Repro environment:
- local-ish: standalone runtime node (g4dn.xlarge equivalent) + nginx reverse proxy in front (emulates LB).
- runtime binary: serving-runtime:main@2026-02-01 build.
- model: opt-2.7b quantized test payload (seq len small, many short replies).
- client: python requests with chunked SSE parser (simple).

Commands / quick repro steps I used:
1) Baseline single-thread stream (works):
python -c "import requests; r=requests.post('http://localhost:8080/v1/streams', json={'prompt':'hey'*5}, stream=True);\nfor chunk in r.iter_lines(): print('CHUNK>', chunk)"

2) Stress repro (concurrency + small back-to-back requests):
# spawn 40 parallel clients sending short prompts in a tight loop (10k requests)
for i in {1..40}; do while :; do curl -s -N -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/streams -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"x"}' & done & done

3) Observed failure surface (collected stderr / proxy logs):
- nginx: "upstream prematurely closed connection (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream" (timestamps align).
- client: got a line like: '{"id":"tok","text":"Hel' (no closing JSON, next line missing).
- server stdout: no stack trace. last trace log: "kv-cache: evict 4 entries; inflight: 38" about 200ms before failure.

Raw snippets captured from one failed stream (client-side):
[RECV LINE 1] : 
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"text":"Hel"},"index":0}],"cursor":"c-123"}
[RECV LINE 2] : 
(data expected) but connection closes immediately after LINE 1

Server debug counters around failure (instrumented logs):
- batching.window_ms=6
- batch_size=1..8 (bursty)
- conn_sendq_bytes avg ~ 3840 for active connections
- kv_cache_hits=0.43, kv_cache_evictions=13 (peak)

What I tried (and quick outcomes):
1) Increased nginx proxy buffer/send timeout to 120s — no change.
2) Disabled nginx keepalive and set proxy_request_buffering off — slight reduction in frequency, not eliminate.
3) Enabled TCP_NODELAY on runtime side (socket option) — reduced incidence by ~60% in short A/B runs. Suggests Nagle interactions.
4) Forced runtime to flush on every token (aggressive) — almost eliminated truncation but throughput dropped 2.7x (not acceptable).
5) Tuned runtime batching.window_ms from 6 -> 2ms — lower latency but increased occurrences (probably more small writes leading to reassembly issues at proxy).
6) Increased send buffer size on runtime process (SO_SNDBUF) — no measurable impact.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) TCP-level coalescing + proxy reassembly bug: Nagle + proxy buffering causes partial frames to be cut when upstream fast-close happens. Evidence: TCP_NODELAY reduced rate.
B) Runtime writes partial SSE event then schedules rest of tokens later; if upstream (nginx) reaches a limit or reorders flushes during backpressure it may close early (connection lifetime mismatch).
C) KV-cache eviction / thrash causes runtime to temporarily block internal worker thread, leading to long pauses between write chunks and causing proxy to consider upstream unhealthy. Note: eviction log ~200ms before.
D) Client SSE parser is fragile (assumes events always newline-terminated). But reproducer using curl also showed truncated payloads, so less likely purely client.

Important error traces and timings (timestamps redacted):
- 10:12:12.433 runtime: wrote 460 bytes to socket for conn cid=0x7f
- 10:12:12.438 runtime: batching: split write, queued next segment (seq 2)
- 10:12:12.640 nginx: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response body from upstream
- 10:12:12.642 client: got single chunk then EOF

Minimal repro script (local, single host) — works intermittently but useful for dev iterate: (put into /tmp/sse-mini-repro.sh)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# spawn 20 concurrent tight requests for ~120s
for n in $(seq 1 20); do 
  ( for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
      curl -s -N -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/streams -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"a"}' >/dev/null 
    done ) &
done
wait

Local experiment notes: run with tcpdump capturing the 1-2 failing sessions and inspect PSH flags; looked like sometimes second segment never had PSH and remote sent FIN after seeing first partial payload.

Short-term mitigations I can apply in prod quickly: 
- enable TCP_NODELAY on runtime listener (rolled to staging; monitor error rate)
- add conservative periodic flush (coalesced) for streaming endpoint that forces finalization of event frame if nothing more after X ms (e.g., 40ms). This was effective in lab.

Longer-term remediation ideas: 
- harden proxy (nginx) to keep upstream alive until full SSE event is complete; investigate proxy buffering edge-case (proxy_request_buffering toggles).
- add a tiny streaming-level sequence checksum/wire-protocol marker so truncated events can be detected and retried gracefully by client.
- instrument and correlate KV cache eviction with streaming events; if eviction correlates, add backpressure hints or prioritize streaming worker threads.

Next short tasks (TODO):
- [ ] Push small flag to enable TCP_NODELAY and run 48h canary on staging (owner: me)
- [ ] Run tcpdump + wireshark on failing session and save 3 PCAPs for ENG-SRE handoff (owner: Yusuf)
- [ ] Add lightweight SSE event boundary metric (emit when first chunk sent vs final chunk) and roll to staging (owner: Lina)
- [ ] Add reproducible harness that asserts full JSON reassembly on curl (owner: me)

Notes for handoff:
- If passing to infra/SRE, highlight timestamps and PCAPs (see linked_artifacts). The issue surfaces when concurrency and evictions align; mention the TCP_NODELAY A/B result.
- If passing to runtime team, point them to batching.window_ms experiments and kv-cache logs.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does tcpdump show no retransmits for the missing segment? Is kernel dropping or are we sending FIN before data drained?
- Are there certain OS-level TCP coalescing settings on our managed instance types that differ between staging and prod?

Appendix: quick python SSE reassembly checker (ad-hoc)
# python snippet to verify whole event present
import requests
r = requests.post('http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/streams', json={'prompt':'x'}, stream=True, timeout=30)
buf = b''
for line in r.iter_lines(decode_unicode=False):
    if not line: continue
    if line.startswith(b'data:'):
        buf += line[5:].strip() + b'\\n'
# simple parse attempt
try:
    import json
    json.loads(buf.decode())
except Exception as e:
    print('reassembly failed', e)

-- end of notes --
